transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-11 15:00 UTC | Duration 54m | Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Narayanan (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jason Li (HighTide CTO), Lila Ramos (Head of Cloud), Carmen Ortega (Security Lead), Tom Nguyen (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto): Joint integration huddle to align on marketplace packaging, VPC/KMS gating, SSO/SCIM, and initial benchmarking plan for a Hybrid LLM gateway. Primary asks: packaging checklist, sample Helm chart values, VPC/KMS validation, and a quick lab benchmark.

Topics: packaging and listing workflow; VPC and KMS gating; SSO / SAML / SCIM for enterprise listing; quantization tradeoffs and perf; canary and routing policies; benchmark plan.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Ethan): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call — we have priya and marco from my side. hi jason, lila, carmen, tom?
00:08 Jason Li (HighTide): yeah hi, thanks for setting this up. we wanted to walk through the marketplace listing flow and nail down networking / kms concerns before we start packaging.
00:15 Priya Narayanan (Redwood SE): awesome. i put a runbook in the chat — redwood marketplace packaging checklist (https://redwood.app/marketplace-checklist) — we'll go through the high level then call out gaps.
00:26 Lila Ramos: perfect. so our goals: one, make sure the connector can run in our staging vpc; two, SSO and SCIM to map groups; three, that the billing/usage metering maps to our internal chargeback.
00:40 Ethan: sounds right. quick context from redwood side: we support hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. for marketplace-listed connectors we ship a Helm chart + operator hooks that your infra team runs, or we can provide an on-prem package if you need air-gapped.
00:55 Tom Nguyen: i saw mention of an operator — we prefer the helm route. our org blocks outbound egress except certain endpoints, so need to know IPs or fqdns to whitelist.
01:05 Marco Ruiz: right, we'll provide endpoints and an optional private control-plane flow. for the marketplace listing with VPC gating we need either a peering or you deploy the connector and we validate via an agent. both work but have different tradeoffs.
01:22 Carmen Ortega: our main infosec questions are KMS integration (customer-managed keys), audit logs retention, and SSO metadata. do you support bringing your own KMS/HSM?
01:32 Priya: yes — BYOK via KMS alias is supported. for on-prem you'd manage the keys; for marketplace we have a flow to attach a customer KMS key through the listing wizard. note: we'll need kms key alias and minimum IAM policy to validate.
01:48 Speaker 2 (Jason): can you show the exact IAM perms? we need specifics for our compliance review.
01:55 Priya: absolutely — i'll attach an example policy in the follow-up. it includes kms:Encrypt/Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, and sts:AssumeRole for the connector role.
02:10 Ethan: let's pivot to packaging. the checklist covers chart-values (image repo, registry creds), and an example values.yaml. we'll also call out a helm hook for canary routing and basePath rewrite so the LLM gateway can be proxied into your existing ingress.
02:28 Lila: on canary routing — how do you recommend splitting between dedicated and shared? some endpoints are high qps and we'd like dedicated capacity for lower tail latency.
02:40 Marco: we typically advise dedicating pools for high qps low latency endpoints and using shared hosted for lower-throughput ones. the routing policy can do percentage-based canaries or route-by-header (e.g., x-tenant-priority).
02:55 Tom: latency numbers? we want to ensure 95th < 300ms for short prompts. is that realistic on your dedicated 8xA100 configs?
03:06 Priya: 95th under 300ms is realistic for sequences under 256 tokens on dedicated pools with batching tuned. there are variables — model size, quantization, and KV cache warmup. our perf profile doc (we'll attach) has baseline numbers.
03:22 Jason: we plan to use an internal medium LLM for most cases. any guidance on quantization impact? lower bits cause hallucinations we want to avoid.
03:31 Priya: great question — 8-bit quant (int8/4bit) often gives 1.8-2.8x token throughput reduction in cost while keeping quality for many open models. but yes, some workloads show small regressions. we'll share a tradeoff matrix.
03:45 Carmen: please label those tradeoffs — we can't take regressions in legal/contract text generation. we might require a canary with automatic fallback to fp16 if quality drifts.
03:58 Marco: we have a rollout policy option to automatically fallback to a higher-precision variant when eval metrics degrade. we wire that to your eval set via a webhook.
04:10 Speaker 3 (Ethan): clarifying — the eval webhook expects a small JSON payload and returns pass/fail. is that what you want for legal flows?
04:18 Carmen: yes — and we will need audit trails for every deployment, including who triggered canaries and where keys were stored. retention is 2 years per our policy.
04:26 Priya: audit logs retention is configurable; for marketplace listings we can surface the audit to your SIEM via syslog/forwarding or push to an S3 bucket encrypted by your KMS.
04:38 Tom: about networking: if we do peering, what IP ranges do we need to reserve?
04:44 Marco: for peering we recommend allocating an /24 for connector egress, but if you're doing private control plane, you can restrict to outbound to our catalog endpoints only. we'll provide exact CIDR and fqdn list in the PR.
04:58 Jason: ok. also curious about upgrades: when the listing updates the helm chart, how do we orchestrate zero-downtime?
05:06 Priya: our helm chart includes a rolling update strategy and pre/post hooks that warm the KV cache. we also support canary release via a weight-based ingress controller annotation, and an automatic failback if latencies spike.
05:22 Ethan: quick note — in some transcripts the team called it KV cash earlier; just to be clear it is KV cache.
05:28 Lila (laugh): heard it.
05:33 Jason: are there any dependencies on specific ingress controllers (nginx vs envoy)?
05:38 Marco: no hard dependency; we provide annotations for nginx, contour, and istio. envoy path rewrite is slightly different but supported. we'll include sample ingress snippets.
05:48 Carmen: what about SSO? we use SAML with ADFS and SCIM for user provisioning. do you support group sync and role mapping?
05:57 Priya: yes SAML & SCIM supported. for marketplace we'll ask for SSO metadata and an attribute mapping file. we can map SAML group to RBAC role so 'legal-review' maps to a restricted policy.
06:12 Tom: any monthly metering hooks if we run in our environment but want to report usage back to Redwood for billing?
06:20 Ethan: yes there's a metering agent that emits deltas to our billing API; for marketplace we bundle it as a sidecar. if you want, you can opt into a push or pull model.
06:30 Jason: that helps. next, bench plan — priya you mentioned a staging lab?
06:35 Priya: yes, propose we run a 1k RPS synthetic run against a medium model in your staging with KV hit rates toggled. we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, cpu and gpu util, and token cost. the plan is about 90 minutes but we'll split into two runs.
06:52 Lila: do you need access to our staging cluster or can you provide an infra-as-code script?
06:58 Priya: either works. preferred is you run the helm chart with our sample values, then we orchestrate the load from our lab account. if you prefer we can run in our sandbox with a mirrored config.
07:12 Tom: we'll probably run in our staging; i'll provision a namespace and share kubeconfig bound to a service account.
07:20 Ethan: sounds good. ACTIONS — i'll send the packaging checklist and sample values; priya will send the benchmark test plan and sample policies; tom will share kubeconfig + VPC details; carmen will send SSO metadata.
07:36 Speaker 4 (Jason): just a note on timeline — we'd like to be listed in the marketplace alpha by end of january. is that doable?
07:42 Priya: january is tight but doable if we get the IDs and VPC info this week and run the lab the week of 12/22. the packaging and legal review can run in parallel.
07:52 Carmen: compliance review requires us to see audit log forwarding and KMS controls; we'll target sign-off 1/10.
07:59 Ethan: good. any other technical risks we should call out?
08:03 Marco: quantization quality for legal text (we flagged) and network egress restrictions are the two big ones. also model compatibility — we'll validate the medium model architecture in our perf lab.
08:15 Jason: competitors — we've looked at sageMaker endpoints and replicate; we like your unified routing and on-prem option.
08:23 Priya: thanks. we'll capture a short comparison doc.
08:28 Lila: ok let's recap next steps and owners.

Recap (auto):
- Redwood: packaging checklist, sample Helm values, quant tradeoff doc, benchmark plan
- HighTide: kubeconfig/namespace, VPC CIDR, SSO metadata, compliance questions
- Target dates: packing checklist 12/12, SSO metadata 12/15, VPC details 12/18, bench plan 12/20, lab run wk of 12/22

Final notes: shared artifacts referenced during call — marketplace checklist (https://redwood.app/marketplace-checklist), perf baseline doc (drive: //shortlink/perf), helm sample values (drive: //shortlink/helm-values).

Meeting end 54:00

Transcription notes: occasional mislabels (Speaker 2/3) and minor word substitution ("KV cash" in one segment). overall usable for follow ups.
